In [[mathematics]], the '''Faxén integral''' (also named '''Faxén function''') is the following [[integral]]<ref>{{cite book|first1=Frank W. J. |last1=Olver |publisher=A K Peters/CRC Press |title=Asymptotics and Special Functions |date=1997 |page=332 |doi=10.1201/9781439864548|isbn=978-0-429-06461-6 }}</ref>
:<math>\operatorname{Fi}(\alpha,\beta;x)=\int_0^{\infty} \exp(-t+xt^{\alpha})t^{\beta-1}\mathrm{d}t,\qquad (0\leq \operatorname{Re}(\alpha) <1,\;\operatorname{Re}(\beta)>0).</math>

The integral is named after the Swedish physicist [[Olov Hilding Faxén]], who published it in 1921 in his PhD thesis.<ref>{{cite thesis|first=Hilding|last=Faxén |type=PhD|publisher=[[Uppsala University]] |title=Einwirkung der Gefässwände auf den Widerstand gegen die Bewegung einer kleinen Kugel in einer zähen Flüssigkeit |date=1921 |url=http://libris.kb.se/bib/8220666}}</ref>

== ''n''-dimensional Faxén integral ==
More generally one defines the ''<math>n</math>-dimensional Faxén integral'' as<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Richard Bruce|last1=Paris|publisher=A K Peters/CRC Press |title=Asymptotic expansion of n-dimensional Faxén-type integrals |journal=European Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics |volume=3 |number=6 |date=2010 |pages=1006–1031 |url=https://www.ejpam.com/index.php/ejpam/article/view/816}}</ref>
:<math>I_n(x)=\lambda_n\int_0^{\infty}\cdots \int_0^{\infty}t_1^{\beta_1-1}\cdots t_n^{\beta_n-1}e^{-f(t_1,\dots,t_n;x)}\mathrm{d}t_1\cdots \mathrm{d}t_n,</math>
with
:<math>f(t_1,\dots,t_n;x):=\sum\limits_{j=1}^n t_j^{\mu_j}-xt_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots t_n^{\alpha_n}\quad</math> and <math>\quad\lambda_n:=\prod\limits_{j=1}^n\mu_j</math>
for <math>x \in \C</math> and
:<math>(0<\alpha_i <\mu_i,\;\operatorname{Re}(\beta_i)>0,\; i=1,\dots,n).</math>
The parameter <math>\lambda_n</math> is only for convenience in calculations.

== Properties==
Let <math>\Gamma</math> denote the [[Gamma function]], then
*<math>\operatorname{Fi}(\alpha,\beta;0)=\Gamma(\beta),</math>
*<math>\operatorname{Fi}(0,\beta;x)=e^{x}\Gamma(\beta).</math>
For <math>\alpha=\beta=\tfrac{1}{3}</math> one has the following relationship to the [[Scorer function]]
:<math>\operatorname{Fi}(\tfrac{1}{3},\tfrac{1}{3};x)=3^{2/3}\pi \operatorname{Hi}(3^{-1/3}x).</math>

=== Asymptotics ===
For <math>x\to \infty</math> we have the following asymptotics<ref>{{cite journal|first1=David|last1=Kaminski|first2=Richard B.|last2=Paris|title=Asymptotics via iterated Mellin–Barnes integrals: Application to the generalised Faxén integral |journal=Methods and Applications of Analysis |volume=4 |date=1997 |issue=3 |pages=311–325 |doi=10.4310/MAA.1997.v4.n3.a5 |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/pages/journals/items/maa/content/vols/0004/0003/a005/index.php}}</ref>
*<math>\operatorname{Fi}(\alpha,\beta;-x)\sim \frac{\Gamma(\beta/\alpha)}{\alpha y^{\beta/\alpha}},</math>
*<math>\operatorname{Fi}(\alpha,\beta;x)\sim \left(\frac{2\pi}{1-\alpha}\right)^{1/2}(\alpha x)^{(2\beta-1)/(2-2\alpha)}\exp\left((1-\alpha)(\alpha^{\alpha}y)^{1/(1-\alpha)}\right).</math>
